0.title: The workflow builder
0.body: This is where you build automations visually: a node palette on the left, the canvas in the middle, a configuration panel per node, and run and validation tools on the right. Let's walk through each part.

1.title: The canvas
1.body: Arrange steps and wire outputs into inputs, then hit run to test the whole flow.

2.title: Triggers start the workflow
2.body: A trigger decides how a run begins — Manual, Webhook, Schedule, Event or Form Input. It's configured like any other node; until one exists, this banner reminds you to add one.

3.title: Workflow-level inputs
3.body: Inputs on a root node (one with no incoming connections) are asked for whenever the workflow runs, so downstream nodes can reference them.

4.title: The node palette
4.body: Browse your Lenses and popular public Lenses here. Each card becomes a node on the canvas; connections between nodes control which data flows where.

5.title: What a Lens contributes
5.body: A Lens-backed node runs that Lens's prompt against a model. Opening a node's configuration panel shows exactly which Lens and version it uses.

6.title: Configuring a node
6.body: Required and optional fields come from the Lens's version parameters, each with its own default. Fill in a value, wire it from an input or an upstream node, or leave the default.

7.title: Node documentation
7.body: Utility nodes expose a docs icon that opens their reference — required fields, formats and examples — without leaving the canvas.

8.title: Validate before you run
8.body: Run a dry run to check the graph for missing fields or bad mappings before spending anything on a real execution. Errors point at the exact node and field responsible.

9.title: Running the workflow
9.body: Pick a funding source and model, then execute from here. Progress, final output and recovery options for a failed run all appear in this panel.

10.title: Run history
10.body: Every past run — its status, duration and node-by-node results — is listed here so you can inspect or compare outcomes.

11.title: Beyond the browser
11.body: The same workflow can also be run, validated and inspected from the CLI (workflow run / validate / create) or through MCP tools, subject to your permissions.
